content.user_title: Create a Storm Survival Story Chapter
content.value_statement: Interactive story writers need a structured way to create urgent survival scenes without losing player choice. This chapter supplies staged dialogue, decision points, and follow-up hooks for a planetary storm scenario.
actual_capabilities: Sets an extreme-storm scenario with a two-hour preparation window.
Guides roleplay as Stella Chen, a survivor on the planet Gaia.
Provides player decision points for shelter, supplies, and storm-eye actions.
Structures the scene into preparation, impact, storm eye, recovery, and aftermath stages.
Offers three ending branches based on survival outcomes and discoveries.
Introduces narrative hooks for intelligent life, stolen equipment, and later chapters.
limitations: It is a narrative writing guide, not real emergency or weather safety advice.
It provides one predefined character, setting, and storm scenario.
It does not execute tools, inspect game state, or track player choices automatically.
The source dialogue is primarily Chinese with some English terms.

use_cases.title: Write a survival roleplay scene
use_cases.description: Use the staged script to run a tense science-fiction survival session with player choices.

use_cases.title: Plan a game narrative quest
use_cases.description: Adapt the preparation tasks, consequences, and endings into a storm-focused game quest.

use_cases.title: Practice dramatic scene pacing
use_cases.description: Study the escalation from warning to isolation, recovery, and a new mystery.

prompt_templates.title: Start the chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Surviving the Storm chapter. Introduce Stella, explain the storm warning, and ask me which preparation priority to choose first.

prompt_templates.title: Choose storm preparations
prompt_templates.prompt: Roleplay Stella during storm preparation. I choose to reinforce the shelter first. Show the immediate tradeoffs and ask for my next decision.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt the storm scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt this chapter for my science-fiction setting. Keep the five-stage structure, but replace Gaia, Stella, and the weather details with my setting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a branching aftermath
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the storm chapter structure to create three distinct aftermath branches. Each branch must have a consequence, a character emotion, and a hook for the next chapter.

output_examples.input: Start the chapter and ask for my first decision.
output: A scanner reports an approaching extreme storm and a two-hour preparation window.
Stella lists shelter, supplies, water, communications, and an emergency plan as competing priorities.
The story asks the player to choose the first priority.

output_examples.input: I choose to inspect the camp during the storm eye.
output: Stella finds major camp damage and scattered cave crystals.
Fresh, unfamiliar footprints create a new mystery.
A scanner warning forces Stella to return before the storm wall arrives.

best_practices: State the player choice clearly before continuing each decision point.
Keep consequences consistent with the selected survival priority.
Use the aftermath discovery to connect naturally to a later chapter.
anti_patterns: Do not present the fictional survival actions as real emergency guidance.
Do not remove every consequence from difficult player choices.
Do not reveal the intelligent-life mystery before the storm aftermath.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It provides a structured interactive science-fiction survival chapter.

faq.question: Is this real weather safety guidance?
faq.answer: No. It is fictional narrative material and not emergency advice.

faq.question: Can I change the setting?
faq.answer: Yes. You can adapt the character, planet, weather, and discoveries.

faq.question: Does it include player choices?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes choices for preparation and the storm-eye period.

faq.question: What happens after the storm?
faq.answer: The chapter offers survival, loss, and mystery branches for the aftermath.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
